title: Police seek witnesses to road struggle
article: Western Communities RCMP want to talk to anyone who saw a man struggling with police and paramedics on the Trans-Canada Highway seconds before his death.

"We're appealing to the public and looking for more witnesses," said Staff Sgt. Bruce Brown. "There was lots of traffic going by. We know there were at least two anonymous 911 calls. There had be somebody who saw something."

Mladen Cujko, 33, of Burnaby, was pronounced dead at Victoria General Hospital at 10:20 p.m. Sunday. He had been picked up by the RCMP after people called to report that a man, yelling and screaming, was running in and out of traffic on Goldstream Avenue at Jacklin Road.
On his way to the hospital in a police car, he became violent and tried to kick out the windows.
After the car was pulled over to the side of the road Cujko got out and started struggling with the police officer on the highway.
Police would also like to talk to anyone who saw Cujko, knew who his friends or acquaintances were, or knew where he was living in the days leading up to his death.
Six Vancouver Island RCMP officers are working on the case and investigating whether drugs were responsible for Cujko's behaviour and death, said Brown.
They are also looking at the similarities between his death and that of a 47-year-old Lower Mainland man who collapsed and died Sunday night after being restrained by Squamish RCMP.
The Capital Health Region has put out a general alert with its street nurses to warn drug users that bad drugs may be on the streets and to take extra care.
